title: Bram and the Thorn
premise: Wren Vane, the crown's food-taster and an orphan raised in the smuggler warrens of the Thornfell mountains, has spent their life being nobody on purpose. But when a scholar's forbidden book reveals a century-old prophecy describing Wren by name, date, and dish, they learn the old kingdom of Velthmar—erased from maps after a coup—sealed a door that only its 'forgotten child' can open. Hunted by the regent's inquisitors who want the door destroyed and by rebels who want it weaponized, Wren gathers a found family of smugglers, exiles, and one repentant inquisitor to reach it first. In the end, Wren discovers the door leads not out of the country but back into its buried heart: opening it restores Velthmar's memory to every citizen at once, toppling the regime not with a sword but with truth—and Wren chooses to stay, no longer invisible, as the new kingdom's first witness.
about_author: Z. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former line-cook turned archivist who grew up in a mining town where half the families claimed descent from a kingdom no map remembered. They write fantasy about people the histories skip, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine morning tasting for the Regent's table establishes Wren's immunity training, their careful anonymity, and their secret knowledge of Thornfell's smuggler roads. When a minor poison nearly kills them anyway, Wren realizes someone inside the palace wants a taster dead. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging—the palace is home and trap at once.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing the kitchens, Wren shelters in the archive of disgraced scholar Ilse Marrow, who shows them a century-old prophetic text naming 'Wren Vane' and tonight's date beside a drawing of a door. Emotional beat: vertigo—the life Wren built on being unremarkable is revealed as scripted by someone long dead.

chapters.title: What the Regent Burned
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse explains the erased kingdom of Velthmar and the purge that followed the coup; her own family was ruined for keeping such books. Inquisitor Captain Dain Rook arrives searching the archive; Ilse burns the prophecy page and tells Wren to run. Emotional beat: grief and urgency—history is a crime scene still smoking.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Spine
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren escapes through Thornfell using routes only tasters and smugglers know, pursued by Rook's hounds. They collide with a smuggling crew led by the irreverent Bram Odell—who claims the mountain roads answer to him. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Wren's invisibility skills become visible value.

chapters.title: The Crew of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduced to the crew: hedge-witch Sefa, mute cartographer Pim, ex-soldier Yara, and Bram himself, who owes a debt to a dead woman named Vane—Wren's mother. Emotional beat: warmth breaking through suspicion; the found family takes shape around a campfire and shared lies.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Pass
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rook corners the crew at a checkpoint; Wren talks them free by posing as his informant, burning their last tie to palace safety. Sefa reads Wren's palm and finds the prophecy's mark already there. Emotional beat: point of no return—Wren chooses the road over the walls.

chapters.title: The Rebel Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crew is captured by Velthmari rebels who believe Wren is the prophesied key and want the door opened to restore the old crown—with themselves enthroned behind it. Their leader, General Corvess, is charming and utterly certain. Emotional beat: dread dressed as rescue; Wren realizes everyone wants to own the door.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvess produces Wren's mother's ledger: she was Velthmar's last royal taster, and she sealed the door herself to keep it from all factions. Wren learns their immunity was never training—it was inheritance, bred for this single purpose. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations; identity as something done to them.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Dark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram bargains with Corvess for Wren's freedom and is refused; he begins planning theft instead, confessing to Sefa why he owes the Vanes. Meanwhile Rook, off-book, sends Wren a coded warning: the Regent knows about the door too. Emotional beat: loyalty crystallizing into love Bram won't name.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captive in the rebel hold, Wren works in its kitchen and quietly poisons the garrison's stores—not to kill, but to sicken and stall, using a taster's craft as resistance. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; justice outside any law, measured in pinches and hours.

chapters.title: Rook's Confession
chapters.summary: Dain Rook's POV. Rook intercepts the fleeing crew alone and, instead of arresting them, reveals he served the purge's archives—he burned Velthmar's records and has doubted it ever since. He offers maps in exchange for being there when the door opens. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution; the enemy becomes a companion.

chapters.title: Thornfell's Heart
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Guided by Pim's recovered maps and Rook's confession, the company crosses the deep mountain to the hidden vale where Velthmar's capital sleeps under stone. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a place Wren has never been but recognizes.

chapters.title: The Door That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. At the door, Sefa deciphers the seal: it opens only for the forgotten child, and what's beyond isn't escape—it's the kingdom's preserved memory, waiting to be poured back into the world. Corvess's rebels arrive armed to seize it. Emotional beat: revelation reframing the whole quest.

chapters.title: Corvess's Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvess offers Wren queenship beside her—a restored throne with Wren as its sanctified symbol. Wren refuses: they've been a tool for the palace, the prophecy, and now the rebellion, and they're done being anyone's instrument. Emotional beat: defiance; power offered and seen clearly as corruption.

chapters.title: Siege of the Vale
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Rebels attack; the crew holds the door chamber in a desperate stand. Yara falls buying time, and Pim speaks their first words in years to guide Wren through collapsing tunnels. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the found family pays in blood for each other's futures.

chapters.title: The Regent Arrives
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Regent herself descends with inquisitors, revealing she is Velthmari nobility who engineered the erasure and will kill the 'key' rather than let memory return. Rook turns his sword against his own order. Emotional beat: terror and clarity—the face of power finally unmasked.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered, Wren uses their final inherited gift: they taste the Regent's poisoned chalice meant for the door's destruction ritual and swap it, letting the ritual consume itself. The Regent's certainty curdles into ruin. Emotional beat: triumph of small crafts over grand cruelty.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Bloodied and grieving, Wren presses their hand to the door and speaks their mother's sealing-words backward. It opens onto Velthmar intact beneath the mountain—streets, songs, ten thousand sleeping memories. Emotional beat: wonder edged with fear of what waking it will do.

chapters.title: The Kingdom Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The memory floods outward through Thornfell into the lowlands: every citizen suddenly remembers Velthmar, the coup, the stolen names. Regime officers drop their weapons mid-order; crowds weep in market squares. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice arriving not as vengeance but as shared remembering.

chapters.title: What We Do With Truth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the aftermath, Corvess tries to claim the restored kingdom by right of blood; the awakened people refuse her, having watched her siege. Rook surrenders himself to a jury of the newly remembering. Emotional beat: hard hope—truth toppled the regime, but building what follows is slower work.

chapters.title: Names on the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren buries Yara, frees Ilse from prison, and carves the fallen crew's names beside the door so no one is ever 'forgotten' again. Bram asks what Wren will do now that the prophecy is spent. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace; the script is finished, the life is their own.

chapters.title: The First Witness
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. A year later, Wren declines every offered title and instead becomes the kingdom's official Witness—keeper of the door and the record, sworn to taste every truth before it's served. Bram stays; the crew becomes family in fact, not just necessity. Emotional beat: quiet joy—an invisible person, finally seen, choosing to be the one who sees.
